isolation: The app holds a single shared, un-sandboxed todo list with no per-scenario container to own. Each scenario creates the specific todo(s) it needs, with distinct titles, via the API (a faster/less brittle way to establish Given state than the UI). Count-based Given/Then pairs (e.g. 'the list has 2 todos' / 'has 3 todos') are judged on the DELTA they claim (+1, -1, unchanged) measured against the count read immediately before the scenario's When, since the shared list already held pre-existing todos from prior runs and could not be reset to an absolute baseline. Only one validation run executes against this deployment at a time, so no concurrent writer could confound the delta.

steps.text: Jamie the user tries to add a todo with a blank title
steps.observed: Add button stayed [disabled] for both an empty value and a whitespace-only value, so the UI itself cannot carry the attempt. Escalated to the API to get the app's own answer rather than relying on the disabled control: curl -s -i -X POST $API/todos -d '{"title":""}' -> HTTP 400 {"code":400,"message":"title must not be blank"}; same 400 for a whitespace-only title. This is the application's own refusal (not a gateway 401), so the scenario is judged on it rather than reported blocked.

steps.observed: count=5, unchanged from the baseline of 5
